name: Customer cannot change another customers order status
description:
Write-side access control: can a user CHANGE something that isn't theirs, or do admin-only actions?

Safety on the shared site: probes that SHOULD be blocked use non-existent ids or empty bodies, so even
when the app is broken nothing real is created or modified. Confirmed app bugs are strict xfails.

statusMessage:
XFAIL BUG: customer B can change customer A's order status via PUT /invoices/{id}/status (found 2026-11-10)

AssertionError: must be refused: 422 {"message":"The status message field must be between 5 and 50 characters.","errors":{"status_message":["The status message field must be between 5 and 50 characters."]}}
assert 422 in (403, 404)
 +  where 422 = <Response [422]>.status_code

api = <toolshop.api.client.ToolshopApi object at 0x76b7df4a3d40>
customer_api = <toolshop.api.client.ToolshopApi object at 0x76b7df4be7e0>
placed_order = {'billing_street': 'Lesingel 8', 'billing_city': 'Steensel', 'billing_state': 'Noord-Holland', 'billing_country': 'NL', ...}
other_customer = Customer(first_name='John', last_name='Davis', email='qa.61a9b66c4e65433fadd97029528bcd7a@example.com', password='xfXM#lDls$&1+u', dob='1990-01-15', phone='0612345678', token=None, id='01m72pfrt6gvm08vzeygsb995v')

    @pytest.mark.progression
    @pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason="BUG: customer B can change customer A's order status via "
                                           "PUT /invoices/{id}/status (found 2026-11-10)")
    def test_customer_cannot_change_another_customers_order_status(api, customer_api, placed_order, other_customer):
        before = invoice_status(customer_api, placed_order["id"])
        other = api.as_token(api.login(other_customer.email, other_customer.password))
    
        r = other.put(f"/invoices/{placed_order['id']}/status", json={"status": "ON_HOLD", "status_message": "x"})
    
        assert invoice_status(customer_api, placed_order["id"]) == before, "another customer changed my order status"
